field_glossary.backend_ladder: Per-backend outcome of the kernel-agent dispatch. ``produced_artifact=false`` across all rows is the dominant signal that the entire ladder failed for this kernel.
field_glossary.bandwidth: Per-case ``bytes`` / ``algbw_gbps`` / ``busbw_gbps`` from the final bench. Latency alone cannot separate a faster transfer from a cheaper barrier; bus bandwidth against the fabric peak says which one a kept kernel bought, and which regime still has headroom.
field_glossary.bound_type: Whether the kernel is limited by memory bandwidth (memory-bound) or compute (compute-bound).
field_glossary.collective_attempt_id: Stable identity for one collective campaign, used to deduplicate resumed or salvaged attempts across a session.
field_glossary.collective_op: The collective primitive that was optimized: ``all_reduce``, ``reduce_scatter`` or ``all_gather``.
field_glossary.compile_passed: True only if at least one backend in the ladder produced a usable patch. False means the whole backend ladder failed to produce any compiled artifact.
field_glossary.e2e_gain_pct: End-to-end throughput delta measured by the integrate gate. This, not micro_speedup, decides whether a collective KEEP is adopted.
field_glossary.efficiency_pct: Achieved throughput as a percentage of the kernel's roofline peak for its bound_type. Lower = more headroom to gain.
field_glossary.gpu_pct: Share of total GPU time spent in this kernel (kernel_duration / total_gpu_duration). Higher = more impactful to optimize.
field_glossary.lane: Which optimization lane produced the row. ``collective`` rows come from the multi-GPU comm lane and carry no roofline geometry, so efficiency_pct / bound_type / arithmetic_intensity stay null.
field_glossary.salvaged: True when the validated best was recovered from the campaign sidecar after the wrapper timed out, rather than returned by a clean exit.
field_glossary.speedup_basis: Whether the row's headline number was validated end to end (``e2e``) or is a microbenchmark ratio only. A collective's microbenchmark routinely overstates its end-to-end worth, so treat ``microbenchmark`` rows as unproven.
field_glossary.world_size: Rank count the collective was measured across; the lane requires it to match the run's TP width.

new_findings.expected_impact: Reframes the search: target per-step decode work, not KV/util tuning.
new_findings.what: Baseline decode step costs 137.8ms at batch 64. Weight-streaming floor for 26.46GiB INT8 on one MI250X GCD (~1.23-1.6TB/s) is ~18-23ms/step, so we are ~6x off the memory roofline => the step is compute/LSU-issue bound, not weight-BW bound. Any lever that cuts per-step bytes-per-token or instruction count is worth more than another weight-BW lever.

new_findings.accuracy_risk: Real: bf16 recurrent state accumulates rounding over long (2048-6144) contexts. Model author shipped fp32 deliberately.
new_findings.expected_impact: Highest-value single byte-reduction available; 5-15% throughput if BW-relevant, more if LSU-bound at locked clocks.
new_findings.what: GDN recurrent (SSM) state cache is float32. text_config.mamba_ssm_dtype='float32' and vllm/model_executor/models/config.py:786-805 (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGenerationConfig) copies it into cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype when that is 'auto'. Size: 48 value heads x 128 x 128 x 4B = 3.1MB/layer x 48 GDN layers = 151MB per in-flight request, read+written every decode step => ~19.3GB/step at conc 64 (~12-16ms/step at BW floor, and fp32 doubles the LSU/vector-register pressure at fixed sclk). --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype is a first-class CLI flag (engine/arg_utils.py:1237, MambaDType=['auto','float32','float16','bfloat16']) and an explicit user override is honoured with only a warning.

new_findings.expected_impact: Potentially larger than all config levers combined; needs Coordinator confirmation because it is a rig property, not a serving flag.
new_findings.what: GPU clocks were reported at sclk 800 MHz / fclk 400 MHz for ALL 1748 monitoring samples across the 3766s baseline run (range '800 - 800'), at a flat 96-98W package power, and a read-only `rocm-smi --showclocks` at idle now still shows sclk level 1 (800MHz) on every GCD. MI250X boost is ~1.7GHz/300W+. If the DPM level is genuinely pinned to min, every compute/issue-bound kernel in this workload pays ~2.1x and no vLLM flag can recover it.

new_findings.expected_impact: Saves ~2 benchmark slots by ruling out the prefill-mixing family.
new_findings.source: runs/baseline/.../server.log loggers.py:310 lines (Avg prompt ~1000-1400 tok/s vs Avg generation ~140-290 tok/s at Running: 64)
new_findings.what: Prefill interference is NOT the bottleneck. At steady state ~70 decode steps + ~2 prefill chunks (max_num_batched_tokens=2048 default, config/scheduler.py:42) fit in a 10s window; solving 70*T_dec + 2*T_pre = 10000ms with T_dec=137ms leaves only ~410ms total for prefill => mixed/prefill steps are ~4% of wall clock. Mean ITL (137.81ms) == mean TPOT (137.81ms) confirms this. Levers aimed at prefill/decode mixing (chunked-prefill budgets, cudagraph_mode for prefill) are low-yield here.

KV cache is NOT the limiter either: 31.96 GiB KV / 292,717 tokens, usage peaked at 58.7%, zero 'preempt'/'retract' occurrences in 2500+ scheduler lines, Running: 64 sustained. '--kv-cache-memory=37216046080 to fully utilize gpu memory' and gpu-memory-utilization tuning will produce 0% because nothing is being evicted.

new_findings.expected_impact: Unlocks a spec-decode lane for future rounds on a prose corpus. NOT proposed this round: the sealed benchmark uses dataset_name='random' and KB law (8) says random corpora collapse acceptance, so it would benchmark as a false negative.
new_findings.what: KB law 'MTP is not built into 0.28.0+rocm723 here' is WRONG for this checkpoint. The target checkpoint SHIPS MTP weights (mtp.fc.weight, mtp.layers.0.{q,k,v,o_proj,q_norm,k_norm,mlp.*}) in model.safetensors.index.json, text_config has mtp_num_hidden_layers=1, and vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py + a registry entry exist. So --speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":N} should load with NO external draft path.

new_findings.expected_impact: Explains why random-corpus A/B is valid for config levers and constrains the prefix-caching proposal.
new_findings.what: The sealed harness benchmark is vllm bench serve with dataset_name='random', random_input_len=1024, random_output_len=1024, random_range_ratio=1.0, max_concurrency=64, ignore_eos=True, num_prompts=320, num_warmups=128 (GEMM/graph-config-valid corpus per KB law (9); invalid for judging spec decode). Prefix cache hit rate reaches 32.8% purely from warmup/main prompt reuse, so --no-enable-prefix-caching has a real prefill cost.

specialist_runs.summary: WIP: baseline decode is 5x off the HBM roofline (TPOT 137.8ms vs ~23-45ms floor); GDN SSM state is fp32 (19.3GB/step traffic) and sclk logged at 800MHz all run. Curating 3-4 variants.

new_findings.expected_impact: Redirects all future recon/patch work to the correct tree; avoids re-proposing an already-bridged switch.
new_findings.what: Live vllm source is /opt/envs/wu1w/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm (launched via /usr/local/bin/vllm-wu1w), which differs from /opt/envs/vllm and already carries a gfx90a AITER INT8 linear bridge: is_linear_enabled() uses is_aiter_attention_supported() (on_gfx9, includes gfx90a) instead of the CDNA3-only @if_aiter_supported. Baseline server.log:28 'Selected AiterInt8ScaledMMLinearKernel' confirms it fires.

new_findings.expected_impact: AITER-tuned Triton attention on the 16/64 full-attn layers at conc=64 decode; explicit --attention-backend bypasses the priority gate and validate_configuration passes for this config.
new_findings.what: ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN never enters candidate backends on gfx90a: platforms/rocm.py _get_backend_priorities only appends it under is_aiter_found_and_supported() = get_cdna_version()>2 (CDNA3+). The backend itself supports head_size>=32 (hd256 OK), block MultipleOf(16) (784 OK), bf16, and runs aiter's Triton unified_attention (arch-neutral, same kernel family as the fallback). Baseline therefore uses ROCM_ATTN whose CK custom paged kernel is rejected at hd256 ('Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation') = generic vLLM Triton for all 16 full-attn layers.

new_findings.expected_impact: Fuses qknorm+rope+reshape_and_cache into one AITER kernel per full-attn layer, removing 3-4 elementwise launches/layer on the decode hot path.
new_findings.what: AITER fused QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache-update pass (fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache, ROCm-gated) is default-False at ALL optimization levels and its last gate is_custom_op_enabled('rotary_embedding') fails because baseline runs custom_ops ['none','+sparse_attn_indexer']. When enabled via -ac it appends '+rotary_embedding' itself and runs QkNormRopeKvcacheFusionPass; the fused op executes via the aiter unified-attn impl's do_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_update (fused_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_supported = rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled(), already true here).

new_findings.accuracy_risk: medium: layout mismatch would corrupt state; kernel source must be read before patching
new_findings.expected_impact: Largest untapped decode lever on this model class (48 GDN layers) if the fused kernels' reshape assumptions hold for non-interleaved packing.
new_findings.what: AITER GDN fused single-token decode fast path (_forward_core_decode_aiter: fused conv1d-update + fused_rearrange_sigmoid_gated_delta_rule, both aiter Triton) is dispatched only when self.gqa_interleaved_layout (Qwen3-Next). Qwen3.5's non-interleaved q/k/v/z packing is explicitly excluded by the gate comment ('Qwen3.5 ... must use the generic path'). 48 of 64 layers are GDN and decode is the dominant regime (conc=64, OSL=1024). Note: vllm _gdn_triton_kernels_importable() probes 'aiter.ops.triton.causal_conv1d_update_single_token' which resolves only via aiter's lazy module map (file lives at aiter/ops/triton/conv/).

proposal_set.name: bridge-rocm-aiter-unified-attn-hd256
proposal_set.reason: Bridge candidate: the aiter Triton unified-attention fast path exists and validates for this model (hd256>=32, block 784%16==0, bf16, causal) but is silently excluded from auto-selection on gfx90a solely by the CDNA3-only is_aiter_found_and_supported() (get_cdna_version()>2) priority gate in platforms/rocm.py:_get_backend_priorities — the same CDNA2-ism the tree already patched around for INT8 linear (is_aiter_attention_supported). Baseline runs generic vLLM Triton attention (CK paged kernel rejected at head_dim 256). Config-only bridge: explicit --attention-backend skips the priority list and goes straight to validate_configuration, which this model passes. If it starts and the log shows 'Using ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN backend (selected via --attention-backend)', the kernel-level A/B for the 16 full-attn layers is live.
source_evidence: session runs/baseline server.log:32,63 (ROCM_ATTN selected; custom paged attn rejected -> Triton)

proposal_set.name: bridge-aiter-qk-norm-rope-kvcache-fusion
proposal_set.reason: Atomic coupled bridge of the AITER fused QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache-update pass: it exists for ROCm+AITER (enable_qk_norm_rope_kvcache = rocm_aiter_ops.is_enabled() && is_custom_op_enabled('rotary_embedding')) but is default-False at every optimization level AND the fused executor (do_qk_norm_rope_kvcache_update) lives on the aiter unified-attn impl, which gfx90a auto-selection silently never picks (CDNA3-only priority gate, see sibling proposal). Both switches must flip together or the pass matches but falls back unfused: (a) --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN; (b) --compilation-config replacing the base one (remove_args drops the inherited flag), keeping cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY and +sparse_attn_indexer, adding fuse_qk_norm_rope_kvcache and +rotary_embedding under the required 'none' base. Fuses 3-4 elementwise kernels per layer on the 16 full-attn layers' decode path.

proposal_set.name: bridge-gdn-decode-aiter-noninterleaved-layout
proposal_set.reason: Bridge candidate for the freeform patcher (no config knob exists): _forward_core_rocm dispatches to the AITER fused GDN decode fast path (fused conv1d-update + fused_rearrange_sigmoid_gated_delta_rule, both aiter Triton, loaded on this box because GDN_AITER_TRITON_AVAILABLE) ONLY when self.gqa_interleaved_layout — i.e. Qwen3-Next. This checkpoint is Qwen3.5 with the non-interleaved q/k/v/z layout ('must use the generic path' comment), so all 48 GDN layers — the majority of the model and the entire decode-critical loop at conc=64/OSL=1024 — take the split/rearrange Triton fallback. The fused_rearrange kernel itself takes generic key_dim/value_dim/head dims (not layout-specific); the layout coupling lives in the fused conv reshape. Patch sketch: extend the dispatch gate for non-interleaved packing (feed it prepare_gdn_attention_core_inputs-style q/k/v slices, or add the qwen3_5 unpack branch inside the aiter reshape), keep gfx90a validation (symmetric bf16 in/out, state fp32/bf16), and A/B under the normal KEEP gate.
source_evidence: session runs/baseline server.log:29-31 (GDN decode kernel: triton)

residual_questions: Record in KB: live tree for this session is /opt/envs/wu1w/.../vllm (vllm-wu1w), already carrying gfx90a AITER-INT8-linear and (per model_arch notes) prior bridges — future recon rounds must grep THAT tree, not /opt/envs/vllm.

Does aiter.ops.triton.conv.causal_conv1d_update_single_token.fused_reshape_causal_conv1d_update_single_token hardcode interleaved qkvz unpacking, or is it parameterized by (num_k_heads,num_v_heads,head_k,head_v) such that Qwen3.5's [k,k,v,v]-shard packing works with adjusted strides? Freeform should read the kernel source before patching candidate 3.

Config-only probe not proposed this round (budget): --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 (GDN conv+ssm states go BF16; FUSED_GDN_STATE_DTYPES allows bf16; bandwidth-bound 48-layer state I/O at conc=64) — worth a slot next round if accuracy gate tolerates; check RecipeKB for prior GDN-state-dtype pitfalls first.

If the unified-attn variant benches positive, should the CDNA3-only gate in _get_backend_priorities be replaced with the gfx9-inclusive is_aiter_attention_supported() (or an arch check inside the backend) as the durable upstream-style bridge instead of the per-launch flag?
